zadanie: Suppose a function $f(x)$ has domain $(-\infty,\infty)$ and range $[-11,3]$. If we define a new function $g(x)$ by $$g(x) = f(6x)+1,$$ then what is the range of $g(x)$? Express your answer in interval notation.
oczekiwana_odpowiedz:
First, note that $f(x)$ and $f(6x)$ have the same range, because every value assumed by $f(x)$ (at, say, $x=a$) is also assumed by $f(6x)$ (at $x=\frac a6$), and vice versa.

Since $g(x)=f(6x)+1$, its range is equal to the range of $f(6x)$ with all values increased by $1$. Thus, the range of $g(x)$ is $[-11+1,3+1] = \boxed{[-10,4]}$.

The new function $g(x)$ is defined as $g(x) = f(6x)+1$. This implies that the input to $f$ is now $6x$ instead of just $x$, and then $1$ is added to the result.

Since the domain of $f(x)$ is $(-\infty,\infty)$, the transformation $6x$ does not change the fact that $f(6x)$ can take on any real value as input. Thus, the domain of $g(x)$ remains $(-\infty,\infty)$.

## Step 4: Determine the effect of the transformation on the range
Given that the range of $f(x)$ is $[-11,3]$, when we apply $f(6x)$, the range remains the same because the transformation $6x$ does not alter the possible output values of $f$. However, adding $1$ to $f(6x)$ shifts the entire range up by $1$. Therefore, the new range becomes $[-11+1, 3+1]$ or $[-10, 4]$.
